one_liner: Cloud accounting software for small businesses with invoicing and payments

evidence.claim: Authentication is OAuth 2.0 with Client ID/Client secret; tokens are required for both sandbox testing and production apps.
evidence.quote: to implement authentication and authorization. Authorization is essential for both testing via sandbox companies and production apps.

evidence.claim: Using the QuickBooks Online API is free; developer credentials are self-serve via the Intuit Developer Portal.
evidence.quote: There is NO COST to connect to QuickBooks Online, or get listed on Apps.com.

evidence.claim: Signing up for an Intuit Developer account is free, giving developers credentials without payment or sales contact.
evidence.quote: Intuit Developer account (free to sign up)

evidence.claim: QuickBooks Online exposes a RESTful accounting API covering company data with full CRUD operations across many objects.
evidence.quote: QuickBooks Online is a cloud accounting platform exposing a RESTful Accounting API for accessing company data programmatically.

evidence.claim: Intuit ships an official MCP server for QuickBooks Online in its own GitHub org (github.com/intuit).
evidence.quote: This MCP server provides complete QuickBooks Online API integration for Claude Code and other MCP-compatible clients.

notes: Official MCP server lives in Intuit's own GitHub org (intuit/quickbooks-online-mcp-server). Gotcha: per an Intuit help thread, production keys now require completing a questionnaire, though development/sandbox keys remain free and self-serve. Official SDKs exist for .NET, Java, PHP, Node.js, Python, and Ruby; access tokens are tied to a company via realmID and use a refresh-token flow.
